documents.CREDITS.md:
# Credits and provenance

The port's reverse-engineering credits and AI disclosure are in the repository
[README](../../README.md#acknowledgements). This scenario and its integration
were developed with AI assistance, continuing the project's work with OpenAI
Sol 6.1 and Astra. No original game source code is included or used as port code.

The nine mech variants are a subset of the existing
[Updated roster](../../content/updated/README.md), adapted from records maintained
by the **MegaMek mm-data contributors**. `sources.json` retains eight pinned source
links/hashes and the initial pack's unpinned Panther URL (no original source hash
was recorded for that entry). `SOURCE-README.md` and `ART-SOURCE-README.md` preserve
the source pack's attribution when exporting this package. Their relative links
refer to the source repository layout. The numeric adapter preserves the pack's armor,
structure, movement, heat sinks, mounted weapons and ammunition. Display names
are expanded from the short labels. Prices remain authored CHI-scale prices;
weapon ranges, damage resolution and rear-weapon behavior use the documented
port adaptations. This is not a claim of complete tabletop equivalence.

The ten vehicle presets come from the repository's editable vehicle catalogue.
[VEHICLE-SOURCE-README.md](VEHICLE-SOURCE-README.md) preserves the Sarna contributor
attribution, individual design links, factual/adapted-stat distinctions and
vehicle-rule limitations. It is copied with the package by New project and
Export. Its repository-relative links refer to the source tree layout.
Their 32-image driving sprites were independently drawn with AI assistance;
no Sarna artwork or original CHI vehicle sprites were copied.

The three ANM portraits are copies of this repository's previously AI-generated
broker, training and ComStar art. Their prompts and production provenance are in
[the art README](../../content/updated/art/README.md); no portrait was extracted
from the original game. Original map tiles, fonts, mech proxy sprites, borders and combat
sound are loaded at runtime from the original files/caches supplied by the player.

The broad setting follows the official descriptions of the
[Lyran Commonwealth](https://battletech.com/factions/lyran-commonwealth/) and
[mercenary commands](https://battletech.com/factions/mercenary/), consulted
2026-10-17. Grayhaven, Beacon Company, its pilots and the contracts are original
fan fiction. The local relay is deliberately described as a local communications
station, not an HPG installation.
documents.LICENSE.md:
# Package licensing

The scenario (`project.json`, `adventure.json`, `contract.lua`), documentation,
and repository-generated portrait and vehicle sprite files (`graphics.json`) are
GPL-3.0-only, to the extent copyright
applies. The full license is [the repository LICENSE](../../LICENSE).

The nine mech definitions in `content.json` contain adapted records maintained by the MegaMek mm-data
contributors. Those adaptations and `sources.json` are provided under
[CC BY-NC-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/4.0/legalcode.en),
as in the existing Updated pack. Attribution, exact sources and the adaptation
limits are recorded in [CREDITS.md](CREDITS.md). The engine's GPL does not
relicense this data.

Vehicle presets use design facts attributed to the Sarna contributors, with
independently authored game adaptations. Their provenance, provisional values
and independently drawn artwork are described in
[VEHICLE-SOURCE-README.md](VEHICLE-SOURCE-README.md).

Original CHI graphics, sound, font, executable and extracted caches are not
included. Players supply those separately. These licenses grant no rights to
the original game assets or BattleTech trademarks. This is an unofficial fan
scenario; its invented settlement, company and events are not canon.
documents.SOURCE-README.md:
# Updated CHI roster — 0.4.0

This optional data pack adds **31 mech models/variants** to the original campaign. Select
**Updated BTECH CHI** before the Westwood/Infocom logo, then enter the central
doorway of Starport's unused three-door building, northeast of Mech-It Lube.
Approach local position **54,50** from the south (**54,51**). Its new **'Mech
Broker** counter has Buy, Sell and Leave options, a descriptive introduction,
compact menu rows and a [newly generated broker portrait](art/README.md).
Delivery uses the existing parked
mech roster; assign a pilot when leaving through the garage (the original
150 C-bill checkout fee still applies). Four owned bays
remain the limit. A free bay and sufficient money are required; rejected
purchases take no money. The Space menu has its original entries.

Updated also supplies new static 1980s anime-style portraits for the Training
Center, lounge, prison, inventor's hut, cinema, hospital, ComStar, clothes shop,
Video Hut and mayor's house. Their
[artwork guide](art/README.md) includes masters, exact prompts, native ANM files
and conversion instructions. Original mode retains the original presentation;
the new art does not change scripts, roster identity or save compatibility.

**Buy a 'Mech** opens four weight classes, with the number of models shown:

| Class | Weight | Stock |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| Light | 20–35 tons | 4 |
| Medium | 40–55 tons | 11 |
| Heavy | 60–75 tons | 12 |
| Assault | 80–100 tons | 4 |

Within each class, models sort by tonnage and then name. **Up/Down scrolls**
one row at a time; Left/Right jumps eight entries. Enter or Space selects.
Back is the last item; Backspace also returns one level, from stock to classes
to the counter. The footer shows the visible range when scrolling is needed.
Save/load preserves the class, highlight, scroll position and pending purchase.
Prices are shown on each row; the selected model's tonnage and movement are
shown below the portrait. Selling still lists your owned bays together.

The broker buys both original and added models. An intact added mech fetches
half its catalogue price; an intact original mech fetches 100 C-bills per ton.
Armor, structure, component, actuator, engine, gyro and sensor damage reduce
the offer. Installed equipment goes with the mech; its crew stays with you.
The confirmation shows the actual offer and defaults to No. Selling frees
that bay without renumbering the other mechs. These are authored expansion
prices, not an original-game mechanic.

The LRM Crusader is the standard mixed-range CRD-3R, not an LRM-only refit.
Charles Bear's documented variant replaces the arm LRMs with SRM-6s and has
18 heat sinks instead of ten. This optional campaign roster does not enforce
historical introduction dates or faction availability.

Phoenix Hawk through Jenner were new in 0.3.0; Shadow Hawk and Rifleman were
already available in 0.2.0. PXH-1 is the conventional Phoenix Hawk, separate
from the original story's Phoenix Hawk LAM. The broker's Jenner also has its
own definition; scripted training Jenners retain their original records.
HGN-733 supplies an AC/10 Highlander compatible with CHI's weapon set; Gauss
rifles are not implemented. The Grasshopper has 22 heat sinks and the Stalker
uses all ten available weapon mounts.

The last eight models are new in 0.4.0. Ostsol and Cicada need no ammunition;
the Ostsol's two rear lasers use ordinary CHI targeting, as with the earlier
rear-mounted weapons. The UrbanMech is a separate broker definition from any
original CHI record. Whitworth's LRMs use the selected Legacy/Enhanced rules.

Catapult, Marauder, Stalker, Jenner and Cicada use the **Locust** sprite;
all other additions use the **red Stinger**. These are the owner's temporary
art choices. Inspection also retains the existing shared CHI diagram, with
armor bars scaled to fit even the Atlas's larger capacities.

Eligible random mech opponents outside Starport can also use these definitions,
so the existing salvage rules provide another acquisition path. Eligibility is
capped at the heaviest owned mech plus 15 tons; an eligible spawn has a one-in-four
chance of using the added roster. Training, scripted fights and arena opponents
keep their existing definitions. This is an optional balance experiment, not an
original-game feature. Prices and ammunition costs are authored for this port.

## Existing Updated saves

New campaigns now start with **Enhanced combat**. Existing saves and imported
Original games retain **Legacy**. To switch outside combat, use **Space →
Change game settings → Combat rules → Enhanced / Legacy**. Progress and owned
mechs are retained. Both manual and automatic LRM shots use the selected
rules; the target panel shows any close-range accuracy penalty.

The optional adjacent [`combat.json`](combat.json) selects the versioned
`chi-updated-lrm-v1` / `weapon-aware-v1` profile. Its range units are the
original effective shot distance divided by three, rounded down and clamped
to one. Minimum range is six; the close modifier is `max(0, 7 - range)`.
Short/medium/long limits are 7/14/21. This is an authored CHI adaptation.
Other weapon ranges retain the original rules. See the
[implementation and evidence](../../docs/MECH_MOVEMENT_AND_LRM_AI.md).

The bounded loader rejects malformed, duplicate or unknown rule fields. A
pack with no `combat.json` remains Legacy. Enhanced saves bind a semantic
rules fingerprint as well as the roster; loading with missing or changed
required rules fails without replacing the current game. Enhanced states
use BTPj/v45 in a BTU2 envelope. Held category menus use BTPk/v46 in BTU2,
including Legacy games with no combat rule file. Ordinary Legacy states keep
BTU1/v44, except while held on the Updated settings pages. These choices share the existing
six Updated slots; no extra save directory is needed.

The first 23 definitions and their save codes are unchanged. Saves from the
released three-model **0.1.0**, 17-model **0.2.0** and 23-model **0.3.0** packs load automatically
in **0.4.0**, including
held broker menus, damage, ammunition, crew and money. No manual conversion is
needed. A held old flat catalogue keeps its original order until you return
to the counter and choose Buy again. Category saves retain the actual selected
model when appended stock sorts before it; Back stays Back. A subsequent save
records the new pack and the state version required by the current screen.

Compatibility is checked by recomputing the saved fingerprint against the
unchanged prefix of the new roster. Editing or removing an existing definition,
changing its ID/code or price, or switching packages still fails explicitly.
This supports appended stock; it is not a general migration for edited mods.
The archived [0.1.0 pack](versions/0.1.0.json), [0.2.0 pack](versions/0.2.0.json)
and [0.3.0 pack](versions/0.3.0.json)
remain available via `--roster` for sessions using an exact earlier catalogue.
Keep earlier save copies if you intend to return to an older pack/executable;
those cannot read saves with the new catalogue identity. The 0.1.0 executable
also cannot read v43 state. Earlier executables cannot read newer v44/v45/v46 states; their
existing saves remain loadable in the current executable.

## Sources and adaptation

Thanks to **MegaMek's mm-data contributors** for the structured unit records:

- [Panther PNT-9R](https://github.com/MegaMek/mm-data/blob/main/data/mekfiles/meks/3039u/Panther%20PNT-9R.mtf)
- [Hunchback HBK-4G](https://github.com/MegaMek/mm-data/blob/main/data/mekfiles/meks/3039u/Hunchback%20HBK-4G.mtf)
- [Catapult CPLT-C1](https://github.com/MegaMek/mm-data/blob/main/data/mekfiles/meks/3039u/Catapult%20CPLT-C1.mtf)

The 28 additions after the initial three use mm-data commit
[`e6f20e1fc2f9d6c74a6e2cdc74778b029ca14811`](https://github.com/MegaMek/mm-data/tree/e6f20e1fc2f9d6c74a6e2cdc74778b029ca14811).
[sources.json](sources.json) records each pinned source URL, SHA-256 and number
of rear-mounted lasers. In particular, the SRM variant comes from
[Crusader CRD-3R (Bear)](https://github.com/MegaMek/mm-data/blob/e6f20e1fc2f9d6c74a6e2cdc74778b029ca14811/data/mekfiles/meks/Force%20Manuals/Mercs/Crusader%20CRD-3R%20%28Bear%29.mtf).
[Sarna's Crusader variants](https://www.sarna.net/wiki/Crusader#Custom_Variants)
provided the initial variant identification; the actual imported statistics
come from the linked unit records.

Consulted 2026-10-16 and 2026-10-17, as recorded for each source. Variant mass,
movement, armor distribution, weapon
locations, ammunition capacities, actuator presence and heat sinks inform this
adaptation. Display names are shortened to fit CHI's 15-character field.
CHI represents weapons with one component descriptor, rather than tabletop
critical-slot footprints; heat sinks are placed in the remaining available
component slots. The 28 later models retain their source heat-sink
locations. Shared ammo bins are divided among matching weapons while preserving
the total number of salvos: the standard Crusader's 15 SRM salvos become 8+7,
and Bear's 45 become 12+11+11+11. CHI reloads each weapon's bin separately.
Rear-mounted lasers use ordinary CHI targeting; rear-only firing arcs are not
represented by this adapter. Original CHI firing, damage, heat and movement
rules apply. Quirks and tabletop construction rules are not implemented.

The adapted [roster.json](roster.json), archived packs and source manifest are separately licensed under
**CC BY-NC-SA 4.0**; see [LICENSE.md](LICENSE.md) and the
[upstream license](https://github.com/MegaMek/mm-data/blob/main/LICENSE).
This data pack is separate from the GPL engine. The new building artwork has its
own [provenance and GPL license notice](art/README.md); it is not adapted from
mm-data. No upstream engine code or artwork, original CHI art, music or
executable is included here. The original
assets must still be supplied by the person running the game. No endorsement
by MegaMek or the BattleTech rights holders is implied.

See [the roster milestone](../../docs/M5A_ROSTER_SLICE.md) for the runtime
format, save compatibility and verification limits.
documents.ART-SOURCE-README.md:
# Updated building artwork

The Updated broker has a new, static portrait of a slick, slightly sleazy male
salesman, following the owner's Jon Hamm / Don Draper suggestion. It was
generated with **Codex's built-in image generation tool** on 2026-10-16.
The original mechanic and weapons-shop portraits supplied local style
references for the 1980s anime/EGA appearance. Those reference images are not
included in this directory or in Git. Seven additional portraits follow the
same style: a veteran instructor, lounge bartender, jailkeeper, inventor,
cinema attendant, clinician and ComStar Adept. These also use the built-in
image generation tool; their exact prompts are in
[building-prompts.json](building-prompts.json).

Three more portraits were generated in built-in mode on 2026-10-17. The clothes
shop has a ridiculous, officious dandy haughtily presenting his clothes. Video
Hut is a 1980s electronics store with an aisle view and a distant clerk, without
Tandy branding. The mayor's house shows a silhouetted intruder in a restrained
futuristic living room with tasteful furniture. Their exact prompts and style
provenance are in [building-additions-prompts.json](building-additions-prompts.json).

Every portrait has a selected `<name>-master.png`, an exact **88×88** indexed
`<name>.png` preview, and a single-frame `<name>.anm` (**3,954 bytes**). The
portraits use 12–14 colors from the game's display palette.

| Building | File stem | Original building ID |
|---|---|---|
| Starport 'Mech Broker | `broker` | 26 (added) |
| Training Center | `training` | 0 |
| Lounge | `lounge` | 7 |
| Prison | `prison` | 13 |
| Inventor's hut | `inventor` | 21 |
| Cinema | `cinema` | 16 |
| Hospital | `hospital` | 9 |
| ComStar | `comstar` | 2 |
| Clothes shop | `clothes` | 12 |
| Video Hut / Frob's Electronics | `video-hut` | 17 |
| Mayor's house | `mayor` | 14 |

Broker files and its original prompt:

- [broker-master.png](broker-master.png): selected generated master.
- [broker.png](broker.png): the exact **88×88**, 12-color in-game image.
- [broker.anm](broker.anm): the same image in the game's native ANM format,
  one frame, 3,954 bytes.
- [broker-prompt.md](broker-prompt.md): the final generation prompt and provenance.

The portraits are newly generated expansion artwork, not recovered CHI assets.
These contributed files use the repository's [GPL-3.0-only license](../../../LICENSE)
to the extent copyright applies. They are separate from the MegaMek-derived
roster data's CC BY-NC-SA license. No rights to the original reference artwork
or BattleTech trademarks are granted.

## Rebuild or replace

Keep an opaque square master. The authoring tool requires Python 3 and Pillow;
the game itself only reads ANM and needs neither Pillow nor a PNG decoder.
From the repository root:

```sh
python3 tools/portrait_convert.py content/updated/art/broker-master.png \
  --output content/updated/art/broker.anm \
  --preview content/updated/art/broker.png
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_portrait.py'
```

Substitute any file stem from the table to rebuild or replace that portrait.

The exporter uses nearest-neighbor reduction and maps pixels to the actual
portrait palette without dithering. Stored index 1 is black, 5 is bright blue,
and 9 is dark blue; treating ANM indices as ordinary EGA would change the colors.
`--resample box` is also available for masters that benefit from area averaging.
Non-square or transparent inputs are rejected so cropping/background choices
remain explicit. The PNG preview and ANM encode exactly the same pixels.

Updated loads these eleven optional `art/<name>.anm` files relative to the
selected **roster JSON file**. Replacing one changes the corresponding building
on the next launch, without rebuilding C, changing mech definitions, or
migrating saves. Each missing file falls back independently to the original
presentation (the mechanic for the broker). An existing but malformed file
rejects the entire edition switch with a named diagnostic, preserving the
previously loaded content. Choosing Original clears all optional portraits.
Art does not contribute to roster identity. The current 0.3.0 roster fingerprint
is **1754795853**; Updated saves remain v43 and Original saves remain v40.
Original O*.ANM files are never replaced.

The renderer displays the last ANM frame as a **static** portrait in the
88×88 building panel. Explicit original BLD animations and their held frames
take priority, preserving the cinema films and other story scenes. Training
quizzes and Katrina's Citadel portrait retain their original presentation.
The eleven assignments above are a bounded filename convention; a general
building manifest/editor and animated custom characters remain future work.

## Verification

**VERIFIED:** the independent Python ANM reader reproduces every exported
four-bit pixel. Actual building visits compare every portrait crop byte-for-byte
with its PNG, exercising the C decoder and renderer palette. The ten ordinary
buildings also compare every pixel outside the portrait with Original, round-trip
held saves, and continue their real BLD scripts with identical state changes.
All ten cinema animation IDs and the training quiz retain Original rendering.
Content tests cover each missing-art fallback, malformed-art rollback, unchanged
roster identity, and switching back to Original.

The bounded window check visits all ten ordinary buildings and verifies their exact
portraits, F5/F9 and the restored full frame on a private display:

```sh
python3 tools/native_smoke.py --building-art-only
python3 tools/native_smoke.py --windows --building-art-only
```

See [the milestone verification](../../../docs/M5A_ROSTER_SLICE.md) for recorded
results. These checks establish the integration; the portraits are authored
interpretations of the buildings, not original-game fidelity claims.

The menu follows the original building presentation: descriptive prose at
the top, `Will you:` and consecutive eight-pixel Buy/Sell/Leave rows. Stock and
sale lists use the same row spacing. Credits, bay occupancy and model details
occupy the lower left panel. Scrolling, confirmations, purchases, sales and
held saves retain their existing behavior. The portrait and dialogue are
**authored expansion content**, not claims of original-game fidelity.
documents.VEHICLE-SOURCE-README.md:
# Editable combat vehicle catalogue

In an authored game project, choose **Import vehicles** in the roster toolbar.
Select the vehicles to import; their weapons, ammunition and original sprite
images come with them. Re-importing preserves existing definitions and artwork.
**Vehicles** in the roster selector shows their movement, five armour facings,
structure and loadout. Right-click the animated preview to edit/select a sprite.

These are playable authoring presets for BtechPort's vehicle adapter. They do
not replace the Original or Updated campaign rosters. Try the
[two-planet proving ground](../../../examples/vehicle-lab/README.md).

## Sources and adaptation

Sarna's contributors provided the reference information below, consulted
2026-10-17. Mass, drive type and principal armament follow the linked standard
design descriptions. Cruise/flank movement points are inferred from their
reported speeds using BattleTech movement conventions. No Sarna prose, artwork,
record-sheet scans or source code was copied into the package.

| Design / source | Tons | Drive | Cruise / flank | Fitted weapons |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: | --- |
| [Patton](https://www.sarna.net/wiki/Patton) | 65 | Tracked | 4 / 6 | AC/10, LRM-5, small laser, flamer |
| [Rommel](https://www.sarna.net/wiki/Rommel) | 65 | Tracked | 4 / 6 | AC/20, LRM-5, small laser |
| [Pegasus](https://www.sarna.net/wiki/Pegasus_Scout_Hover_Tank) | 35 | Hover | 8 / 12 | Two SRM-6s, medium laser |
| [Skulker](https://www.sarna.net/wiki/Skulker_(Combat_Vehicle)) | 20 | Wheeled | 7 / 11 | Medium laser |
| [Drillson](https://www.sarna.net/wiki/Drillson) | 50 | Hover | 9 / 14 | Large laser, LRM-10, two SRM-2s, two machine guns |
| [Galleon](https://www.sarna.net/wiki/galleon) | 30 | Tracked | 6 / 9 | Medium laser, two small lasers |
| [Scorpion](https://www.sarna.net/wiki/Scorpion_(Combat_Vehicle)) | 25 | Tracked | 4 / 6 | AC/5, machine gun |
| [Vedette](https://www.sarna.net/wiki/Vedette) | 50 | Tracked | 5 / 8 | AC/5, bow machine gun |
| [LRM Carrier](https://www.sarna.net/wiki/LRM_Carrier) | 60 | Tracked | 3 / 5 | Three LRM-20s |
| [SRM Carrier](https://www.sarna.net/wiki/SRM_Carrier) | 60 | Tracked | 3 / 5 | Ten SRM-6s |

**APPROXIMATE:** armour totals are 232/176/104/72/116/56/64/96/48/48 in
table order. The Drillson value is inferred from its ferro-fibrous armour mass;
the last four totals are provisional presets. Facing splits use a front bias;
structure, per-mount ammunition allocation, prices and remaining construction
details are editable adaptation choices, not audited record-sheet reproductions.
No chassis mass/critical-slot construction calculator is provided yet.

The vehicle rules distinguish tracked/wheeled/hover movement, five damage
facings and motive damage. They forbid jumping/kicking, suppress mech heat and
avoid mech limb/gyro destruction. This is an explicitly approximate ruleset:
turret rotation/firing arcs, detailed crew/engine criticals, skid/flip rules and
full tabletop vehicle construction are not implemented. Weapon locations affect
damage/critical handling but do not constrain firing arcs. The existing CHI
planner accepts at most 12 steps per movement order, including the Drillson's
nominal 14-point flank allowance. See the
[implementation limits](../../../docs/M5_VEHICLES_AND_PLANETS.md).

## Artwork and reproducibility

`graphics.json` contains independently drawn 32x32 RGBA sprites. Each has eight
directions (N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W, NW) with four driving frames per direction.
Tracks, wheels or hover skirts distinguish the drive types; the art is a
starting point for editing, not a claim to match official vehicle illustrations.

The generator and this original artwork were created with AI assistance and
are distributed under this repository's GPL-3.0-only licence. BattleTech design
names remain attributed to their respective owners. Original CHI assets are
not included here.

To regenerate the shipped presets and demonstration (overwrites those files):

```sh
python3 tools/make_vehicle_catalogue.py
python3 tools/make_vehicle_demo.py
```

The graphics generator requires Pillow. Work on a project copy when editing
art or stats you want to keep; regeneration is unnecessary for normal editing.
